SHANGHAI, August 29th, 1939

To the Commissioner of Police
S.M.P.
Shanghai

Dear Sir:-

Mr. YORKE was good enough to inform me over the
'phone today, that the matter of Documents of Identificat_
ion, which I had submitted to you on the 25th inst. had
been taken under advisement and that a decision would be
given in about two weeks.

In this connection I would like to add to what I
have already said that the German Consulate General has
requested us to deliver to them all " Staatenlose " Passports,
issued by the German Government, which had expired and lost
their validity.

There are quite a number of such Passports now
expired, but we have the greatest possible difficulties
in getting their owners surrender these to us, because, as
I have stated in my previous letter, they would be left
without any kind of a Document.

Were it possible to replace these Passports with our
Document of Identity and were it possible to make these
Documents serve the same purpose as a "Staatenlose" Passport
or a Nansen Passport serves, the difficulties we are meeting
with now would be, I hope, eliminated and, at the same time,
a useful service performed for the people concerned.

Yours faithfully,

"I.C." RELIEF FUND
〔签名〕
Hon. Secretary & Treasurer

（印：Int. Comm. for Ref. I. C.）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 31 AUG 1939）

上海，1939年8月29日

致警务处处长
上海公共租界工部局警务处
上海

尊敬的先生：

约克（Yorke）先生好意于今日通过电话告知我，我于本月25日提交给阁下的身份证明文件一事已获受理，预计约两周后将作出决定。

在此方面，我想补充我之前所述内容：德国总领事馆要求我们将所有由德国政府签发、已过期并失效的“无国籍”（Staatenlose）护照移交给他们。

目前已有相当数量的此类护照过期，但我们在让持照人向我们交还这些护照时遇到了极大的困难，因为正如我在前一封信中所述，交还后他们将没有任何形式的证件。

如果可以用我们的身份证明文件替换这些护照，并使这些证件起到与“无国籍”护照或南森护照相同的作用，那么希望我们目前遇到的困难得以消除，同时也为相关人员提供了有益的服务。

此致
敬礼

“国际委员会”救济基金
〔签名〕
荣誉秘书兼司库

（印：Int. Comm. for Ref. I. C.）
（印：上海工部局总监办公室 1939年8月31日）

SHANGHAI, ......25th August....1939

To the Commissioner of Police
S.M.P.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

You will probably recall that the Council some-
time ago invited me to join a Study Commission dealing
with Emigrant problems.

Mr. F.A.Pitts was, on behalf of the Police a
member of this Commission and, at one of the meetings,
the question of "Staatenlose" persons was brought up and
a discussion arose as to what was best to be done with
these people who, on the expiry of their Passports would
have no such document because renewal was declined by
the German Consulate.

Seeing that there is also no Nansen office here,
I suggested that this Committee issue booklets of Identi-
fication. Mr. Pitts had discussed the matter with some
of the Consulates who said, that if the Police stamped
the booklets, visas, if practicable, would be issued to
other countries.

On the strength of this and also because the
absolute necessity arose I had booklets printed of which
I enclose a specimen.

I might add that, in a recent interview, the
German Consul Mr. E.v.Randow suggested that we should do
something in order to provide identification documents
to those without a country and I was in a position to tell
him, that we had already taken suitable steps in this
direction.

The other day, it being necessary to have a
Document such as this one stamped, the owner had some
difficulty in getting such a stamp. I rang up Mr. Pitts
who told me, to the best of my recollection, that the
matter of stamping was alright only that it had not yet
been decided as to what fee would be charged for the
services in this connection.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 26 Aug. 1939）

However, in conversation with Mr. Wittingsky this
afternoon I was given to understand that instructions
had been given, not to stamp these documents at all.

That would be contrary to arrangement which, to
the best of my knowledge and belief, had been arrived at
and which was a suitable solution of a very difficult

-2-

上海，1939年8月25日

致警务处处长
上海公共租界工部局警务处
上海。

尊敬的先生，

您可能还记得，工部局前一段时间曾邀请我加入一个研究移民问题的专门委员会。

皮茨（F.A.Pitts）先生代表警务处担任该委员会成员，在一次会议上，提出了关于“无国籍”（Staatenlose）人员的问题，并讨论了如何最好地安置这些人，因为他们的护照到期后将没有此类文件，德国领事馆拒绝予以延期。

鉴于此地也没有南森办事处，我建议本委员会签发身份证明小册子。皮茨先生已与一些领事馆讨论过此事，他们说，如果警务处在小册子上盖章，在可行的情况下，将向其他国家签发签证。

基于此，也由于绝对必要性的出现，我印制了小册子，随函附上样本一份。

我还要补充一点，在最近的一次面谈中，德国领事冯·兰多（E.v.Randow）先生建议我们应采取行动，为无国籍人士提供身份证明文件，而我能够告诉他，我们已在此方向采取了适当措施。

前几天，因需要在此类文件上盖章，持有人在获取此类印章时遇到了一些困难。我致电皮茨先生，据我回忆，他告诉我盖章事宜没有问题，只是尚未决定对此项服务收取多少费用。

（印：上海工部局总监办公室 1939年8月26日）

然而，今天下午在与维廷斯基（Wittingsky）先生交谈时，我获悉已下达指令，根本不在这些文件上盖章。

这将违背据我所知和所信已达成的安排，而该安排本是解决一个非常困难的

-2-

SHANGHAI, 25th August, 1939

problem.

Personally, I see no reason why such endorsement
by the Police should not be given seeing that the autho_
rities and Consulates accept our and only our endorsement
in other matters concerning Emigrants.

The matter of a Document of Identification is an
urgent one to such persons who, for one reason or another
have lost their citizenship. Without such a document
some of these people feel absolutely lost. It robs them
of some form of security which they, with a Passport or
a substitute for the same, feel.

At the same time, such a Document offers, as I
have indicated, a possibility for them to go to other
countries f.i. to Tientsin, Tsingtau etc. and it is urgent_
ly necessary that people should have every opportunity to
leave Shanghai, if such opportunity offers itself.

Mr. Freund, whose Document I attach, wishes to
leave for Tsingtau or Tientsin and with the Police stamp_
ing the Passport, he can get a Japanese permit on the basis
of permit obtained by us through our corresponding Committees
in the northern Ports.

I trust therefore, that the arrangement which had
been, as I believe, arrived at, will not be now cancelled
and I request that you be so good as to give the necessary
instructions to your sub_organs for the endorsements to
be accorded when called for.

I beg to remain,

Dear Sir,

Yours faithfully,

上海，1939年8月25日

问题。

就我个人而言，我看不到警务处为何不应给予此类背书，因为在涉及移民的其他事项上，当局和领事馆只接受我们的背书。

对于那些因某种原因失去国籍的人来说，身份证明文件之事迫在眉睫。没有这样的文件，这些人中的一些感到完全迷失。这剥夺了他们拥有一本护照或其替代品时所感受到的某种安全感。

同时，正如我所指出的，此类文件为他们前往其他国家（例如天津、青岛等）提供了可能性，因此，如果有机会离开上海，人们迫切需要有各种机会这样做。

附件中是其证明文件的弗罗因德（Freund）先生希望前往青岛或天津，只要警务处在护照上盖章，他就可以凭我们通过北方港口对应委员会获得的许可，取得日本方面的许可证。

因此，我相信此前已达成的安排不会被取消，并恳请阁下向您的下属机构发出必要指令，以便在需要时给予背书。

谨此奉达，

尊敬的先生，

此致
敬礼

page_data.en:
CCY

S. Ishiguro, Esq.,
Consul for Japan,
Shanghai

Dear Mr. Ishiguro,

Re: Immigration

From the "8-Uhr Abendblatt", an emigrant evening paper, of April 23, I learn that 1,000 immigration permits for Hongkew residents are about to be issued. The issue of 20th April of the same paper contains a notice, telling applicants when to apply (according to the alphabet) to the Japanese Consulate General for delivery of the landing permits already referred to. All these applications were submitted without the intermediary of our Committee, so that the latter was not enabled to investigate the bona fides of the applicants; nor could we examine the prospects of the new arrivals to make a living in Shanghai.

While welcoming the idea to help people to get out from Central Europe and enable them to start life afresh in a new land, we feel apprehensive as to the ability of the newcomers to stand on their own feet. Since November last year, when immigration was again permitted under certain restrictions, our Committee has carefully examined the statements made in writing by applicants and has invariably passed on such requests only, which contained a fair chance that the newcomers will not become a burden to either our Committee, or to the Shanghai community at large.

Recently the Electionscreening Association, consisting of refugees, a body without juridical standing, has inaugurated a campaign for the issue of immigration permits. We have no desire whatsoever to either criticize, nor to interfere in any way with the decisions of your Consulate General in this respect. On the contrary, we really remain thankful for the great kindness you have displayed towards the unfortunate masses of citizens who are forced to abandon their homes. But on the other hand, I feel dutibound to place on record that :
(a) our Committee cannot accept responsibility for the bona fides of both the applicants and the immigrants, as long as the applications have not been passing through our hands for examination of the statements contained therein.
(b) that, in the event of emigrants arriving here without means - especially if this happens in large numbers - our Committee will most likely be unable to take them to the Homes and maintain them there for a lengthy period of time.

Bringing to your notice for your kind consideration the contents of this last paragraph is really the main purpose of this letter. The means at our disposal are dwindling as time goes on and I fear that we should not be able to cope with the requirements of a large mass of people landing here without means and being unable to care for their own support.

This does not mean that our Committee does not want to see an increase in the size of the refugee population here. As a matter of fact, we at all times welcome the growth of the migrants colony in China and shall gladly place our advice and assistance at its disposal. But what circumstances demand is that newcomers ought to be able to stand on their own feed and not be dependent upon the very slender monetary resources of our committee.

I thought it advisable to bring to your kind notice these actualities and desire to thank you once more for the very helpful consideration which you hitherto have been good enough to devote to a really worthy cause.

Believe me, dear Mr. Ishiguro,

Very sincerely yours,
Ed. E. Kann
page_data.zh:
CCY

致石黑 S. Ishiguro 先生，
日本驻上海领事，
上海

尊敬的石黑先生：

事由：移民

我从4月23日的移民晚报《八点钟晚报》（8-Uhr Abendblatt）获悉，即将向虹口居民签发1,000份移民许可证。该报4月20日的一期刊登了一则通知，告知申请人何时按字母顺序向日本总领事馆申请领取前述登陆许可证。所有这些申请均未通过本委员会中介提交，因此本委员会无法调查申请人的诚意；我们也无法审查新来者在上海谋生的前景。

虽然我们对帮助人们从中欧出来并使他们在新土地上重新开始生活的想法表示欢迎，但我们对新来者自力更生的能力感到担忧。自去年11月在某些限制下再次允许移民以来，本委员会仔细审查了申请人提交的书面陈述，并且仅转呈那些新来者不太可能成为本委员会或整个上海社区负担的请求。

最近，由难民组成的“选举筛选协会”（Electionscreening Association，一个没有法律地位的团体）发起了一场运动，要求签发移民许可证。我们绝无意批评或以任何方式干涉贵总领事馆在此方面的决定。相反，我们真的感谢您对被迫离开家园的不幸民众所表现出的巨大善意。但另一方面，我觉得有责任记录在案：
(a) 只要申请未经过我方之手以审查其中包含的陈述，本委员会就不能对申请人和移民的诚意承担责任。
(b) 如果移民身无分文抵达此地——尤其是如果这种情况大量发生——本委员会很可能无法将他们收容至收容所并长期维持其生活。

提请阁下注意最后一段的内容确实是本信的主要目的。随着时间的推移，我们要支配的资金日益减少，我担心我们将无法应对大量身无分文且无法自食其力的人在此登陆的需求。

这并不意味着本委员会不希望看到此地难民人口增加。事实上，我们始终欢迎中国移民聚居地的增长，并乐意提供建议和援助。但形势要求新来者应能自立，而不依赖本委员会非常有限的资金资源。

我认为将这些实际情况提请阁下注意是明智之举，并再次感谢您迄今为止对这一真正有价值的事业所给予的极具帮助的关注。

相信您，亲爱的石黑先生，

您最诚挚的，
Ed. E. Kann
